**Top of mind:** Amazon pulled out of both ends of the AI-data value chain this week — it shut its 18-month-old AGI Lab on July 24 with layoffs hitting post-training and model-customization teams, and Mechanical Turk closes to new customers on July 30. Meanwhile India-side consolidation is real: EXL's up-to-$310M acquisition of iMerit heads toward a Q3 close, putting a public price tag on India-heavy annotation delivery.

## Competitor moves

- **EXL is acquiring iMerit for up to $310M; British International Investment announced its exit as the deal heads to a Q3 2026 close.** A US-listed enterprise data/AI services firm buying one of India's best-known annotation shops sets a valuation benchmark for India-delivery businesses — and integration churn at iMerit opens a window to court its enterprise clients and senior delivery talent. [BII](https://www.bii.co.uk/en/news-insight/news/british-international-investment-to-exit-imerit-following-a-period-of-growth-and-impact/)
- **Amazon Mechanical Turk stops accepting new customers this Thursday, July 30 — AWS has moved the 21-year-old platform to maintenance mode with no new features planned.** The original commodity-crowdwork marketplace is effectively dead; its academic and SageMaker Ground Truth requester base will need managed alternatives, which favors vendors with low-cost, quality-controlled India delivery. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/05/amazon-will-stop-accepting-new-customers-for-mechanical-turk/), [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/07/03/amazons-mechanical-turk-to-stop-accepting-new-customers-and-not-even-ai-can-save-it/5266274), [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/07/05/amazons-mechanical-turk-service-now-life-support-stops-accepting-new-users/)

## New projects & opportunities

- **Amazon is redirecting AGI budget into enterprise deployment, including a reported $1B program embedding AWS engineers with customers building agentic AI systems.** Enterprise agent rollouts at that scale need domain-specific evals, guardrail datasets and trajectory QA — a services surface a data vendor can pitch alongside AWS partners rather than to frontier labs. [GeekWire](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-cuts-jobs-in-agi-group-as-it-puts-more-focus-on-customer-facing-ai/), [TNW](https://thenextweb.com/news/amazon-shuts-agi-lab-frontier-model-retreat-layoffs)
- **MTurk's July 30 cutoff creates an immediate migration pipeline** — displaced requesters (universities, survey platforms, ML teams on Ground Truth) are choosing replacements over the next quarter; fast, low-friction onboarding and academic pricing could capture this long tail. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/05/amazon-will-stop-accepting-new-customers-for-mechanical-turk/)
- No fresh India-specific RFPs or tenders verified in the last 48 hours.

## Frontier lab movements

- **Amazon closed its AGI Lab (July 24) after cutting roughly 10% of the AGI group on July 22, with reductions concentrated in model customization and post-training.** The clearest signal yet that Amazon is exiting the frontier-model race — one fewer potential whale buyer of post-training data, with its spend shifting to customer-facing AI and $200B of infrastructure. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/22/amazon-lays-off-some-employees-in-its-agi-unit.html), [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/07/23/amazons-agi-department-finds-humans-are-optional/5276874), [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/321341/20260723/amazon-cuts-agi-jobs-while-pouring-200-billion-ai-infrastructure.htm)
- **SpaceXAI (xAI's new name since July 6) launched Grok 4.5 trained on Cursor developer-session data, and says Grok 4.6 lands within about two weeks.** The strategic read for data vendors: labs with product telemetry (Cursor sessions, SpaceX engineering corpora) are substituting it for purchased annotation — commodity labeling loses, but expert evals and red-teaming for domains telemetry can't cover (legal, finance were Grok 4.5's launch verticals) gain. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-08/spacexai-cursor-unveil-grok-ai-model-for-legal-finance-tasks), [Trending Topics](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/spacexai-and-cursor-launch-grok-4-5-not-yet-in-the-eu/), [NextBigFuture](https://www.nextbigfuture.com/2026/07/spacexai-will-release-grok-4-6-in-2-weeks-and-grok-4-7-in-4-weeks.html)

## Research papers

- **TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents (submitted July 15)** — Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Tao Ge, Hao Cheng, Mike Hang Wang, Jianfeng Gao and Sharon Li. Derives per-turn rewards for agent trajectories spanning hundreds of tool calls instead of relying on sparse outcome labels — a preview of what labs will ask vendors to produce next: turn-level reward and QA annotation on agent rollouts, not just final-answer grading. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13988)
- **Process Reward Informed Tree Rollout (PATR) for multi-turn agent RL (arXiv, mid-July; anonymous, under review)** — uses process scorers on partial trajectories to decide where to branch rollouts. Every scheme like this needs calibrated process-reward labels and graders, reinforcing process-supervision data as a growth line alongside RL environments. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15610), [OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=mj6Ho1bjY5)

## Research papers

- **CRAFT: Clustering Rubrics to Diagnose Weak LLM Capabilities and Generate Targeted Fine-Tuning Data (arXiv, July 22).** Clusters grading rubrics to find where a model is weak, then generates fine-tuning data aimed at exactly those gaps — a template for selling "diagnostic + targeted data" packages instead of undifferentiated volume. Authors listed on the arXiv page. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16122)

[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15092), [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12835)

## Research papers

- **"Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training" (Shen, Li, Rahman, Sun, Goldblum, Telgarsky, Izmailov — NYU; #2 Hugging Face paper of the day, July 20).** Using chess and math as controlled testbeds, they show post-RL performance is well-predicted by pretraining loss, and that on hard problems RL surfaces correct behaviors nearly absent from the SFT policy rather than just sharpening it. Practical read: pretraining data quality directly sets the ceiling on RL returns, and hard-case data — the expensive, expert-authored kind — is where RL creates new capability. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16097), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.16097)
- **"Recursive Harness Self-Improvement" (Hyunin Lee, Jinglue Xu, Jeffrey Seely, Donghyun Lee, Matei Zaharia, Yujin Tang — Sakana AI, July 17).** Frames agent harnesses as data-generating components whose execution traces feed future model training, and shows a few self-refinement iterations lift low-effort agents past max-effort baselines at up to 60% lower inference cost. Signal for the data business: agent execution traces are becoming first-class training data — trace curation, grading, and QA is a sellable pipeline stage. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15524), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/2607.15524)

## Research papers

- **"Debiasing Text-to-Image Evaluation via Implicit Cultural Alignment Reward Modeling" (arXiv, July 2026).** Culturally aligned reward modeling for image evaluation is exactly the kind of work that requires diverse, non-Western annotator pools — a defensible niche for India-based, multilingual/multicultural rater networks. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15740)
- **"From Holistic Evaluation to Structured Criteria: Rubrics Across the Evolving LLM Landscape" (arXiv, June 2026).** Surveys the shift from holistic judging to rubric-based evaluation — rubric authoring by domain experts is a growing, higher-margin service line than plain preference labeling. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.08625)
